question.problem: Find the acute angle between the vectors $v=[\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{2} \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

current_example.problem: Find the acute angle between the vectors ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14156912/assets/a7e1c024cac9597bbb899c2d73a374922b552c58e184c7f0a5f92fc77dd3d774.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14156912/assets/c1addab7256bd5919d108d7ef64a9b1a2bde2781e2553ea9a416ce8223ecf988.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Using the formula

$$
\cos\theta = \dfrac{\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{w}}{\Vert\mathbf{v}\Vert \, \Vert \mathbf{w}\Vert},
$$

we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 2+(-4)\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot 2}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\,\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{10}{\sqrt{25}\cdot \sqrt{16}} \\  & =\frac{10}{5\cdot 4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta=\arccos \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}.
$$
